claims.text: A metadynamics-assisted adaptive thermodynamic-integration framework can replace full-scale explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics free-energy evaluations.
The proposed framework will substantially reduce the computational cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties in multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The proposed framework will retain vibrational entropy contributions faithfully.
The proposed framework will retain anharmonic contributions faithfully.
The proposed framework will retain electron–vibration coupling contributions faithfully.
Metadynamics will bias the system to overcome free-energy barriers and accelerate phase-space sampling.
Accelerated phase-space sampling will enable efficient exploration of rare phase-transition events.
Improved sampling will reduce the number of required ab initio evaluations.
The method may reduce computational cost by approximately an order of magnitude.
The method will provide fidelity comparable to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
The method will scale better than TOR-TILD for multicomponent systems.
First-principles calculations for multi-principal-element alloys are computationally demanding.
Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows accurately compute solid and liquid free energies but are computationally demanding.
TOR-TILD becomes substantially slower for compositionally complex high-entropy systems.
The proposed method is expected to work near melting temperatures for elemental systems, binary alloys, and high-entropy alloys.
Performance and accuracy outside the fusion regime or beyond the stated compositional range have not been validated.
The attainable speedup and fidelity depend on system complexity and on whether the sampling captures all relevant entropy contributions.
Rare-event dynamics may remain unresolved in extremely multicomponent mixtures.
